articles.title: How Payhawk raised $280m amid fintech downturn
Goldman Sachs leads $280M funding round in Payhawk
Bulgaria’s first unicorn Payhawk raises €255.14 million at €1.82 billion valuation in Goldman Sachs-led Series C round

brief.essentiel: Payhawk , a London-based AI-native spend management platform, today announced a €255.14 million ($280 million) Series C round, valuing the business at €1.82 billion ($2 billion) as it builds the global finance operating system (OS) for the AI era.
points: This round brings the company’s total funding to more than $515 million.
In March 2022, it raised an additional €89 million and extended its funding to €191 million, making it Bulgaria’s first unicorn .
In November 2021, the company raised €99 million in Series B funding, valuing it at €505 million.
It raised €16.5 million in Series A in April 2021 and €3 million in a Seed round in March 2020.

articles.title: 8 key findings from Atomico’s State of European Tech report
5 key findings from Atomico’s State of European Tech 2026

brief.essentiel: Europe’s tech ecosystem is heading for its second-best investment year on record, with bigger funding rounds, a new generation of founders and startups scaling at unprecedented speed.
points: Among the standout deals are UK-based Wayve’s €1 billion Series D to scale AI-powered autonomous driving, German DefenceTech startup Quantum Systems’ €1 billion Series D , and British AI voice company ElevenLabs’ €424 million Series D .
Standout examples include Mistral AI’s €3 billion Series D and Nscale’s €1.7 billion Series C .
During the first nine months of 2026, approximately €18 billion ($20 billion) flowed into European AI and compute companies , compared with €258 billion ($284 billion) in the United States.

But the continent’s structural weaknesses remain: venture capital is increasingly concentrated, the US is pulling ahead in AI investment, and European companies still struggle to access growth capital.

articles.title: Opinion: Maintaining the open web is central to Europe’s AI sovereignty ambitions

brief.essentiel: Europe’s ambitions for AI sovereignty depend on giving its startups the resources to succeed, innovate and compete with established companies.
points: As it stands, the EU remains heavily reliant on digital technologies developed and managed from elsewhere, raising questions about its ability to control the systems underpinning its economy.
In June this year, the European Commission unveiled its European Technological Sovereignty Package .
The Tech Sovereignty Package also aims to fast-track the implementation of the European Commission’s existing AI Continent Action Plan.
This includes the Cloud and AI Development Act, which specifically aims to support the research, development and innovation of next-generation AI technologies, including frontier AI models.

articles.title: EIT Jumpstarter recognises Europe’s most promising early-stage innovators of 2026 (Sponsored)

brief.essentiel: The EIT Jumpstarter 2026 winners have been announced, recognising a new generation of entrepreneurs developing solutions to some of Europe’s most pressing healthcare, food, energy, mobility and industrial challenges.
points: The winners were revealed during the EIT Jumpstarter 2026 Awards Ceremony, held at Unicorn Factory Lisboa in Lisbon, as an official side event of Web Summit.
Selected from a pool of 895 applications, the winning teams developed their ideas through training, mentoring, market validation and pitch development.

Since its launch, EIT Jumpstarter has trained more than 1,500 innovators, supported the creation of over 150 startups, contributed to more than 2,600 jobs and helped participating companies attract over €150 million in external investment.
Their solutions span a wide range of sectors, including nanotechnology, food and AgriTech, energy, shared mobility, geoscience and other innovative technologies addressing real-world challenges.
